senses.sense_definition: In Aristotelian ethics, a condition of living a life of the highest virtue; the state of human flourishing and true well-being desirable for its own sake.

examples.text: Aristotle argued that true <w>eudaimonia</w> requires both intellectual and moral virtue.
Modern philosophers often translate <w>eudaimonia</w> as human flourishing rather than mere happiness.

senses.sense_definition: One of the Charites (Graces) in Greek mythology, representing happiness and prosperity.

examples.text: In ancient Greek art, <w>Eudaimonia</w> is depicted alongside the other Charites bringing joy to mortals.
The poet invoked <w>Eudaimonia</w> to bless the newlyweds with prosperity and happiness.
